rv.q: The utter cruelty of Carlos and the stoic resolve of Gladys, in the hands of Duque-Estrada and Iglesias, especially in a critical moment like this, is majestic.
But once his juices are flowing, it seems that on almost every line he switches which two characters are allied against the odd one out.
If only the dialogue and events in the first act were less wooden, the characters more nuanced, and the issues more developed. But it all feels uncomfortably like a mediocre TV family drama.
